title: Returning Carrier-Imposed Taxes on an Unflown Air Ticket Fare Brands Ticket
content:
A ticket sold under the Air Ticket Fare Brands that has fallen away unflown still carries carrier-imposed taxes and fees which the airline itself returns. This is the entry point for putting that money back on the card the traveller paid with.

## 1. The situation this governs

The situation is an Air Ticket Fare Brands booking whose ticket has fallen away without being flown. The result governed is the sum returned to the form of payment the traveller used, and the effect the traveller sees is a payout line standing on the booking, a lower net paid total, and the money on the card statement the airline settles it to.

## 2. The write that records it

The return is made by the desk. The agent-side tool `return_unflown_taxes_e343d675` is unlocked and then called; one call posts a single payout line to that booking's ledger for the stated sum, marks it as money going back to the original form of payment, dates it on today's business date and lowers the booking's net paid total by the same sum.

## 3. Parameters

- `air_booking_id` — the internal reference number of the air booking whose taxes are returned, read from the traveller's booking record returned by the booking lookup. An identifier.
- `customer_id` — the traveller reference number the payout line is recorded against, read from the traveller profile returned by the profile lookup. An identifier.
- `payout_amount_usd` — the sum returned to the card, in USD with exactly 2 decimal places, stated as a positive number and rounded to the nearest cent at the moment it is passed; there is no empty value and no other currency.

## 4. What comes back

A plain-language confirmation line naming the reference of the payout line that was posted, the sum returned in USD to two decimal places, and the booking's net paid total once the payout landed. The presence of that line reference is what indicates the money was sent back; nothing is returned when no line is posted.
